source.title: PAC Bayesian Performance Guarantees for Deep (Stochastic) Networks in Medical Imaging
source.authors: Anthony B. Sicilia; Xingchen Zhao; Anastasia Sosnovskikh; S. Hwang

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material supplied
record.tranche_reason: The study varies prior variance and reports how stochastic-network performance changes, using a different procedure from the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares PAC-Bayes and Hoeffding performance guarantees; those comparisons do not measure a claim version's named behavior. Cited results from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study investigates PAC-Bayes guarantees and sensitivity to Gaussian prior scale. It does not measure V7's relationship between magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and measured training–test gaps, or test any other version. Its broader flat-minima motivation and variance-sensitivity results do not establish that relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find non-vacuous PAC-Bayes guarantees competitive with Hoeffding guarantees on the studied medical imaging tasks, and interpret prior-scale sensitivity as suggesting a flatter minimum for U-Net than for LW or ResNet-18. Effectiveness in substantially smaller datasets remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PAC-Bayes with backprop to train stochastic networks and varies prior variance to probe performance; it does not use magnitude-scaled weight perturbations to rank generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Prior variance changed the reported performance trend: U-Net remained stable before a drop at σp = 0.04, while LW and ResNet-18 degraded as variance grew.

fits_no_version.finding: U-Net maintains high holdout DSC and a high PAC-Bayes lower bound through σp = 0.03 before dropping at 0.04; LW and ResNet-18 degrade as prior scale increases. The authors interpret this as evidence of different local flatness, assuming runs remain near the same minimum.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sensitivity of retrained stochastic predictors to Gaussian prior scale can probe local loss-landscape flatness on medical imaging tasks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
record.problems: The variance-sensitivity results are primarily described through plots, with no numerical values or uncertainty reported for the trends. The study does not directly measure training-to-test gaps or use magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.rows_left_out: Section 3.2 also compares PAC-Bayes and Hoeffding bounds and reports holdout performance as comparable; these results concern the guarantees, not a version's named behavior, so no rows were extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

The entire specified relationship: magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus measured generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted V7 limits_scope verdict. Sensitivity to increasing perturbation scale is not evidence that the specified sharpness–generalization-gap relationship fails or needs qualification.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness with norm- or margin-based measures, or test the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN settings without augmentation.

rows.subject: U-Net (UN)
rows.size_stated: fully-sized U-Net; parameter count not stated
rows.stage_stated: trained 120 epochs; posterior trained for the remaining 90 epochs after prior training
rows.operation_detail: Varied prior variance across runs and assessed performance and PAC-Bayes lower bound.

conditions.value: σp varied; stable performance before the drop at σp = 0.04

rows.measure: Holdout Dice similarity coefficient and PAC-Bayes lower bound
rows.value: Consistently high DSC and a high lower bound before the drop at σp = 0.04; the authors conclude a flat minimum proportional in size to σp = 0.03.
rows.locator: Section 3.2, Flat Minima and Their Size; Figure 1b
rows.note: Precise values are shown only in Figure 1; the text describes the trend and conclusion.
rows.check: Holdout DSC and a PAC-Bayes lower bound do not measure the V7 correlation. Perturbations are not scaled to weight magnitudes, and posterior means and covariances are retrained across runs. The reported stability through σp = 0.03 and drop at 0.04 match the text, but σp denotes prior standard deviation; the variance is σp².

rows.subject: LW

rows.operation_detail: Varied prior variance across runs and assessed performance and PAC-Bayes lower bound.
rows.measure: Holdout Dice similarity coefficient and PAC-Bayes lower bound
rows.value: The authors report consistent performance degradation as prior variance grows and suggest the minima may not be as flat.
rows.locator: Section 3.2, Flat Minima and Their Size; Figure 1c
rows.note: The reported trend is textual; precise values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Degradation in holdout DSC as prior scale grows cannot establish or contradict V7. No magnitude-aware sharpness or measured training–test gap is reported. Each run retrains the posterior. The degradation matches the text; σp is standard deviation rather than variance.
